subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers replace the stale dirty fork PR with a fresh same-repo fix, adopt/rebase that fork PR, or keep waiting on the fork branch for this issue?
rationale: The bug is clear, but an open conflicting fork PR still uses closing syntax for this issue, so automation should not create another fix PR until maintainers choose the branch path.

options.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
options.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

options.title: Adopt Or Rebase Fork PR
options.body: Have a maintainer or contributor update the fork PR to current main, add missing coverage and proof, and review it as the landing candidate.

options.title: Keep Waiting On Fork PR
options.body: Leave the issue blocked on the existing fork PR even though it is dirty and has not updated since April 2026.

recommendation.title: Replace With Fresh Narrow Fix
recommendation.body: Close or supersede the stale fork branch and land a focused same-repo fix covering metadata stripping plus sync and async displayName hydration.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is the committer on the original session-title and TUI picker work and is the strongest routing signal for deciding the branch path.
